narrative:

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were your class rank in the third year of law school, your LSAT score, and your family income bracket. Your third-year class rank was the strongest influence, followed closely by your LSAT score; both pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Your family income had a smaller but still noticeable effect that actually pulled slightly in the other direction.

Your performance placed you in the bottom decile for grades in both your first and third years of law school, far below the average of accepted students who typically ranked around the middle of their class. Similarly, your LSAT score of 20 is well below the average of 37 seen among accepted applicants. These two academic signals were the main reasons the model concluded you were likely to struggle with the bar exam. Your lower-middle family income, while less common among accepted students, slightly improved the outlook but was not enough to offset the academic concerns.

To improve your chances, focus on strengthening your academic record and consider retaking the LSAT to raise your score. These steps would directly address the factors that most influenced the current prediction. (218 words)
